# Introduction
***

<br>

This document provides the fully reproducible analysis pipeline for the manuscript  
*“Estimation of Mortality via the Neighborhood Atlas and Reproducible Area Deprivation Indices”* (Gladish, Phillips, & Rehkopf; JAMA Network Open; 2025).  

The Area Deprivation Index (ADI) is a factor-based measure of neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage originally developed by [Singh (2003)](https://ajph.aphapublications.org/doi/pdf/10.2105/AJPH.93.7.1137) from 17 census-derived indicators of income, education, housing, and employment. The [Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI)](https://www.neighborhoodatlas.medicine.wisc.edu/) later operationalized this index using [American Community Survey (ACS)](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/data.html) data and has been widely adopted in health services research and federal payment models.

Subsequent work has shown that the NA-ADI departs from the original ADI methodology in several important ways, including incorrect application of factor-analytic weights [Petterson; 2023](https://academic.oup.com/healthaffairsscholar/article/1/5/qxad063/7342005), use of outdated weights across time, and minimal updating of variable thresholds. These issues distort deprivation estimates, particularly in high-cost urban and some rural areas, with implications for equity-focused policy and funding decisions [Hannan et al.; 2023](https://www.healthaffairs.org/doi/10.1377/hlthaff.2022.01406?url_ver=Z39.88-2003&rfr_id=ori%3Arid%3Acrossref.org&rfr_dat=cr_pub++0pubmed).  

The [Reproducible Area Deprivation Index (ReADI)](https://sepi.stanford.edu/available-socioeconomic-position-indices/reproducible-area-deprivation-index-readi) is a corrected and fully transparent implementation of the ADI framework. The construction of ReADI is documented in detail in the ReADI methods script [ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd](https://github.com/ngladish/ReADI/blob/main/2018-2022/ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd). This document focuses solely on comparing the resulting ReADI scores with NA-ADI and other indices and evaluating their association with mortality. In brief, ReADI:

- Recomputes factor weights using contemporaneous ACS data at each geographic level.
- Standardizes all component variables prior to factor analysis.
- Updates key thresholds (eg, education and income disparity) to reflect current socioeconomic conditions.
- Produces block-group, tract, and county scores with complete, open documentation and code.  

This R Markdown file:

1. Imports previously generated ReADI scores, official NA-ADI scores obtained from the Neighborhood Atlas, calculated NA-ADI components, mortality data, and other deprivation indices used in the manuscript.  
2. Merges these measures with mortality data and relevant covariates.  
3. Quantifies agreement and systematic differences between ReADI, NA-ADI, and other indices (e.g., distributional comparisons, rank shifts, geographic patterns).  
4. Evaluates each index’s ability to predict mortality using regression and risk-stratification analyses.  
5. Generates all tables, statistics, and figures reported in the manuscript, along with supplementary diagnostics illustrating how differences between indices may affect policy decisions and resource allocation.

All paths are relative to this repository, and all analyses are designed to run from a clean R session on any machine with the required packages installed.

# Methods
***

<br>

## Data Sources
### NA-ADI
***

<br>

We use the official Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI) national percentile scores (0–100) at the census block group (CBG) level for 2015 (v3.1) and 2022 (v4.0.1), downloaded directly from the [Neighborhood Atlas](https://www.neighborhoodatlas.medicine.wisc.edu/). Because the Atlas only distributes CBG-level scores, we construct tract- and county-level NA-ADI values by computing population-weighted averages of CBG scores using ACS total population (table [B01003_001](https://www.socialexplorer.com/data/ACS2022_5yr/metadata/?ds=ACS22_5yr&table=B01003)).

Suppressed CBGs coded `"GQ"`, `"GQ-PH"`, `"PH"`, `"QDI"` (and for 2015 also `"NONE"`) are treated as missing (NA) and excluded from aggregation.

Accessing ACS data via the Census API requires an API key, which can be requested [here](https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html). Once you receive your key, install it in your R environment as the `CENSUS_API_KEY` environment variable (for example, via `.Renviron`) and **do not** hard-code the key in shared code.

For the **2018–2022** analyses we use NA-ADI at the CBG, tract, and county levels.  
For the **2011–2015** mortality analyses we use NA-ADI at the tract level only.

#### 2018-2022 

> Census block group (official source)

The code below:
- Reads the official 2022 NA-ADI CBG file from GitHub (exported from the Neighborhood Atlas),
- Ensures a 12-digit CBG GEOID, and
- Recodes the suppressed categories as missing, resulting in 6,384 NA values and 235,952 CBGs remaining.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code199">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code199" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
NA_ADI_CBG_2022 <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/NA_ADI/2018-2022/US_2022_ADI_Census_Block_Group_v4_0_1.csv", colClasses = c(FIPS = "character"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Sanity checks: FIPS is already a 12-digit unique ID per row
stopifnot(all(nchar(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$FIPS) == 12), 
length(unique(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$FIPS)) == nrow(NA_ADI_CBG_2022))
NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID <- NA_ADI_CBG_2022$FIPS
NA_ADI_CBG_2022$ADI_NATRANK[NA_ADI_CBG_2022$ADI_NATRANK %in% c("GQ", "GQ-PH", "PH", "QDI")] <- NA
NA_ADI_CBG_2022$ADI_NATRANK <- as.numeric(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$ADI_NATRANK)
names(NA_ADI_CBG_2022)[names(NA_ADI_CBG_2022) == "ADI_NATRANK"] <- "NA_ADI"
NA_ADI_CBG_2022 <- NA_ADI_CBG_2022[complete.cases(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$NA_ADI),]
save(NA_ADI_CBG_2022, file = "NA_ADI_CBG_2022.RData")
```
  </div>
</div>

<br>

> Census tract (population-weighted from CBG)

For tract-level NA-ADI scores in 2022, we:
1. Use ACS 2022 B01003_001 to obtain CBG-level population counts,
2. Within each tract, compute CBG-specific weights as the proportion of tract population residing in each CBG, and
3. Compute the tract-level NA-ADI as the population-weighted mean of the CBG NA-ADI scores (`NA_ADI`).

This results in 83,722 census tracts with tract-level NA-ADI scores.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code234">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code234" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load("NA_ADI_CBG_2022.RData")

#Basic sanity checks on NA_ADI_CBG_2022
stopifnot(all(c("GEOID", "NA_ADI") %in% names(NA_ADI_CBG_2022)),
  is.character(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID),
  is.numeric(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$NA_ADI) || is.logical(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$NA_ADI))
# Check Census API key
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY"))) {
  stop(
    "Census API key not found.\n",
    "Please set the CENSUS_API_KEY environment variable (e.g. in .Renviron) ",
    "before running this document.\n")}

states <- setdiff(unique(fips_codes$state_code), c("60", "66", "69", "74", "78")) # Removing US territories

ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG <- do.call(rbind, lapply(states, function(st) {
    get_acs(
      year       = 2022,
      geography  = "block group",
      state      = st,
      key        = Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY"),
      variables  = "B01003_001")
  }))
ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG <- reshape2::dcast(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG, GEOID + NAME ~ variable, value.var = "estimate")
ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT <- substr(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID, 1, 11)
ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_C <- substr(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID, 1, 5)
ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG <- ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG[ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID %in% NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID,]
sum(is.na(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$NA_ADI))
stopifnot(identical(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID, ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID))
save(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG, file = "ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG.RData")

# Sanity: every NA-ADI CBG should have a population row
stopifnot(all(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID %in% ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID))

PopSize_CT <- tapply(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$B01003_001, ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(names(PopSize_CT), unique(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT)))
CT_weight <- ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$B01003_001 / PopSize_CT[ match(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT, names(PopSize_CT)) ]
w_sums <- tapply(CT_weight, ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
if (any(abs(w_sums - 1) > 1e-6)) {
  warning("Some tract-level weights do not sum to 1 (tolerance 1e-6).")
}

NA_ADI_CT_2022_vec <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(NA_ADI_CBG_2022)), ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT, function(idx) {
    weighted.mean(x = NA_ADI_CBG_2022$NA_ADI[idx], w = CT_weight[idx], na.rm = TRUE)})
NA_ADI_CT_2022 <- data.frame(GEOID  = names(NA_ADI_CT_2022_vec), NA_ADI = round(as.numeric(NA_ADI_CT_2022_vec)), row.names = NULL)
if (any(is.na(NA_ADI_CT_2022$NA_ADI))) {warning("Some tract-level NA-ADI values are NA after aggregation.")}
save(NA_ADI_CT_2022, file = "NA_ADI_CT_2022.RData")
```
  </div>
</div>

<br><br>

> County (population-weighted from CBG)

County-level NA-ADI scores are constructed analogously: we aggregate CBG scores within each county using population-weighted means based on ACS 2022 B01003_001, treating suppressed CBGs as missing and excluding them from the weighted averages.

There were a total of 3,214 counties resulting from this.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code599">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code599" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load("NA_ADI_CBG_2022.RData")
load("ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG.RData")

PopSize_C <- tapply(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$B01003_001, ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_C, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(names(PopSize_C), unique(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_C)))
PopSize_C <- data.frame(GEOID_C = names(PopSize_C), PopSize_C = as.numeric(PopSize_C), row.names  = NULL)
ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG <- plyr::join(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG, PopSize_C, by = "GEOID_C")
ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$C_weight <- ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$B01003_001/ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$PopSize_C
# Check weights: should sum to ~1 within each county
w_sums <- tapply(ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$C_weight, ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_C, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
if (any(abs(w_sums - 1) > 1e-6)) {
  warning("Some county weights do not sum to 1 (tolerance 1e-6).")
}
sub_weights <- ACS_2022_PopSize_CBG[, c("GEOID", "GEOID_C", "C_weight")]
NA_ADI_CBG_2022 <- plyr::join(NA_ADI_CBG_2022, sub_weights, by = "GEOID")
# Sanity: every NA-ADI row should now have a county and weight
stopifnot(!any(is.na(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID_C)),
  !any(is.na(NA_ADI_CBG_2022$C_weight)))

NA_ADI_C_2022_vec <- tapply(1:nrow(NA_ADI_CBG_2022), NA_ADI_CBG_2022$GEOID_C, function(idx) {
  weighted.mean(x = NA_ADI_CBG_2022$NA_ADI[idx], w = NA_ADI_CBG_2022$C_weight[idx], na.rm = TRUE)})
NA_ADI_C_2022 <- data.frame(GEOID = names(NA_ADI_C_2022_vec), NA_ADI = as.numeric(NA_ADI_C_2022_vec),  row.names = NULL)
NA_ADI_C_2022$NA_ADI <- round(NA_ADI_C_2022$NA_ADI, digits = 0)
# Quick sanity: no all-NA tracts created by aggregation
if (any(is.na(NA_ADI_C_2022$NA_ADI))) {
  warning("Some county-level NA-ADI values are NA after aggregation.")
}
save(NA_ADI_C_2022, file = "NA_ADI_C_2022.RData")
```
  </div>
</div>

#### 2011-2015

For the mortality analyses, we use publicly available CDC mortality data through 2015, which are provided at the census tract level. To align with this, we reconstruct 2015 NA-ADI tract scores from the official CBG-level NA-ADI (v3.1) and ACS 2011–2015 population data.

> Census Block Group (official source)

We:
- Download the official 2015 NA-ADI CBG file (v3.1) from the Neighborhood Atlas,
- Convert suppression codes (`"GQ"`, `"GQ-PH"`, `"PH"`, `"QDI"`, `"NONE"`) to `NA`, and
- Save the cleaned CBG dataset as `NA_ADI_CBG_2015` for use in the tract-level aggregation below.

There were 5,323 CBGs with NAs leaving 215,010 CBGs for analysis.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code354">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code354" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
NA_ADI_CBG_2015 <- read.table("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/NA_ADI/2011-2015/US_2015_ADI_Census_Block_Group_v3.1.txt", sep = ",", header = T, row.names = 1, colClasses = c(FIPS = "character"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Sanity checks: FIPS is already a 12-digit unique ID per row
stopifnot(all(nchar(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$FIPS) == 12), 
length(unique(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$FIPS)) == nrow(NA_ADI_CBG_2015))
NA_ADI_CBG_2015$GEOID <- NA_ADI_CBG_2015$FIPS
NA_ADI_CBG_2015$ADI_NATRANK[NA_ADI_CBG_2015$ADI_NATRANK %in% c("GQ", "GQ-PH", "PH", "QDI", "NONE")] <- NA
NA_ADI_CBG_2015$ADI_NATRANK <- as.numeric(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$ADI_NATRANK)
names(NA_ADI_CBG_2015)[names(NA_ADI_CBG_2015) == "ADI_NATRANK"] <- "NA_ADI"
NA_ADI_CBG_2015 <- NA_ADI_CBG_2015[complete.cases(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$NA_ADI),]
save(NA_ADI_CBG_2015, file = "NA_ADI_CBG_2015.RData")
```
  </div>
</div>

<br>

> Census Tract (population-weighted from CBG)

Using ACS 2011–2015 total population (B01003_001), we:
1. Obtain CBG-level population counts,
2. Compute within-tract CBG weights as the proportion of tract population in each CBG, and
3. Aggregate CBG NA-ADI scores to the tract level via population-weighted means, excluding suppressed CBGs.

These tract-level 2015 NA-ADI scores are then merged to the CDC mortality data for the 2011–2015 analyses.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code581">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code518" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load("NA_ADI_CBG_2015.RData")

#Basic sanity checks on NA_ADI_CBG_2022
stopifnot(all(c("GEOID", "NA_ADI") %in% names(NA_ADI_CBG_2015)),
  is.character(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$GEOID),
  is.numeric(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$NA_ADI) || is.logical(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$NA_ADI))

states <- setdiff(unique(fips_codes$state_code), c("60", "66", "69", "74", "78")) # Removing US territories
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG <- do.call(rbind, lapply(states, function(st) {
    get_acs(
      year       = 2015,
      geography  = "block group",
      state      = st,
      key        = Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY"),
      variables  = "B01003_001")
  }))
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG <- reshape2::dcast(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG, GEOID + NAME ~ variable, value.var = "estimate")
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT <- substr(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID, 1, 11)
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_C <- substr(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID, 1, 5)
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG <- ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG[ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID %in% NA_ADI_CBG_2015$GEOID,]
save(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG, file = "ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG.RData")

# Sanity: every NA-ADI CBG should have a population row
stopifnot(all(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$GEOID %in% ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID))

PopSize_CT <- tapply(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$B01003_001, ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(names(PopSize_CT), unique(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT)))
PopSize_CT <- data.frame(GEOID_CT = names(PopSize_CT), PopSize_CT = PopSize_CT, row.names  = NULL)
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG <- plyr::join(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG, PopSize_CT, by = "GEOID_CT")
ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$CT_weight <- ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$B01003_001/ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$PopSize_CT
# Check weights: should sum to ~1 within each tract
w_sums <- tapply(ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$CT_weight, ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG$GEOID_CT, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
if (any(abs(w_sums - 1) > 1e-6)) {
  warning("Some tract-level weights do not sum to 1 (tolerance 1e-6).")
}
sub_weights <- ACS_2015_PopSize_CBG[, c("GEOID", "GEOID_CT", "CT_weight")]
NA_ADI_CBG_2015 <- plyr::join(NA_ADI_CBG_2015, sub_weights, by = "GEOID")
# Sanity: every NA-ADI row should now have a tract and weight
stopifnot(!any(is.na(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$GEOID_CT)),
  !any(is.na(NA_ADI_CBG_2015$CT_weight)))

NA_ADI_CT_2015_vec <- tapply(1:nrow(NA_ADI_CBG_2015), NA_ADI_CBG_2015$GEOID_CT, function(idx) {
  weighted.mean(x = NA_ADI_CBG_2015$NA_ADI[idx], w = NA_ADI_CBG_2015$CT_weight[idx], na.rm = TRUE)})
NA_ADI_CT_2015 <- data.frame(GEOID = names(NA_ADI_CT_2015_vec), NA_ADI = as.numeric(NA_ADI_CT_2015_vec),  row.names = NULL)
NA_ADI_CT_2015$NA_ADI <- round(NA_ADI_CT_2015$NA_ADI, digits = 0)
# Quick sanity: no all-NA tracts created by aggregation
if (any(is.na(NA_ADI_CT_2015$NA_ADI))) {
  warning("Some tract-level NA-ADI values are NA after aggregation.")
}
save(NA_ADI_CT_2015, file = "NA_ADI_CT_2015.RData")
```

### ReADI 
***

<br>

Full, step-by-step construction of ReADI—including variable definitions, formulas, imputation, and factor loadings are documented in:

- **ReADI 2022:** [`2018-2022/ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd`](https://github.com/ngladish/ReADI/blob/main/2018-2022/ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd)  
- **ReADI 2015:** [`2011-2015/ReADI_2015_Creation.Rmd`](https://github.com/ngladish/ReADI/blob/main/2011-2015/ReADI_2015_Creation.Rmd)

This document does **not** recreate ReADI; it only loads these precomputed scores.

#### 2018-2022

For the main analyses we use 2018–2022 ReADI at the census block group (CBG), census tract (CT), and county levels. These are loaded from the public ReADI repository:

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code462">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code462" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/ReADI/main/2018-2022/ReADI_CBG_2022.RData"))
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/ReADI/main/2018-2022/ReADI_CT_2022.RData"))
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/ReADI/main/2018-2022/ReADI_C_2022.RData"))
```

#### 2011-2015
***

<br>

For the mortality analyses, we use ReADI at the census tract level for 2011–2015 to align with the mortality follow-up window.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code470">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code470" class="collapse">

### Other indices (2018–2022)
***

<br>

For external comparison, we use four additional indices: the [Social Vulnerability Index (SVI)](https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/place-health/php/svi/index.html), the [Social Deprivation Index (SDI)](https://www.graham-center.org/maps-data-tools/social-deprivation-index.html), the [Neighborhood Stress Score (NSS7)](https://www.mass.gov/files/documents/2017/11/07/social-determinants-of-health-faq.pdf), and a [French Deprivation Index–style measure (FDep)]((https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2458-9-33). All four are created or obtained in:

- [NSS7_FDep_SDI_2022_Creation.Rmd](https://github.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/Other_Indices/NSS7_FDep_SDI_2022_Creation.Rmd)

Below we summarize how each index is used in this analysis.

> SVI

We use the CDC/ATSDR [Social Vulnerability Index (SVI)](https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/place-health/php/svi/index.html) as an external benchmark. SVI is a composite index developed by the CDC/ATSDR Geospatial Research, Analysis, & Services Program (GRASP) to quantify social vulnerability to disasters and public health emergencies at the census tract and county levels. It is based on 16 variables grouped into four themes (socioeconomic status, household characteristics, racial/ethnic minority status & language, and housing type & transportation) and reported as national percentile ranks from 0–1 (higher = more vulnerable).

In this analysis, we:

- Download the **2022 SVI** at **census tract** and **county** levels from the [CDC/ATSDR SVI website](https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/place-health/php/svi/svi-data-documentation-download.html).
- Use the **overall national percentile score** (`RPL_THEMES`) as the primary SVI measure.
- Assign each census block group (CBG) the SVI value of its county so that all CBGs within a county share that county’s SVI score.

We do **not** recalculate or modify SVI components; all SVI values are taken directly from the official CDC/ATSDR releases. Full methods are described in the CDC/ATSDR SVI documentation.

> SDI

We use a reproduced [Social Deprivation Index (SDI)](https://www.graham-center.org/maps-data-tools/social-deprivation-index.html) as a comparator. SDI was originally developed by [Butler et al., 2012](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1475-6773.2012.01449.x), [Phillips et al., 2016](https://www.healthaffairs.org/doi/10.1377/hlthaff.2016.0709), and the Robert Graham Center to summarize area-level social deprivation from seven ACS-derived indicators (poverty, low education, non-employment, renting, crowding, single-parent families, and no vehicle access) using factor-analytic weights.

Here, we:

- Construct the seven SDI components from ACS 5-year data using the documented Census tables and formulas.
- Fit a one-factor model and use the factor score coefficients as weights to form a composite SDI score.
- Express SDI as national percentile scores (0–100), with higher values indicating greater deprivation.

These SDI scores are a fully reproducible implementation based on the public SDI methodology. They are **not** the official Robert Graham Center SDI release but are intended as a high-fidelity approximation for side-by-side comparison with ReADI, NA-ADI, and other indices.

> NSS7

We include a reproduced [Neighborhood Stress Score (NSS7)](https://www.mass.gov/files/documents/2017/11/07/social-determinants-of-health-faq.pdf) as another comparator. NSS7 is an economic stress measure originally developed for MassHealth by [Ash et al.](https://repository.escholarship.umassmed.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7d562e5-9bf0-4e41-bf5b-c67809e7272d/content), based on seven census-derived indicators at the neighborhood (CBG) level: poverty, ≤200% FPL, public assistance, unemployment, no vehicle access, single-parent families, and low education.

In this analysis, we:

- Construct the seven NSS7 component percentages from ACS 5-year data at the CBG level using the published Census tables and formulas.
- Standardize each component, sum the seven z-scores, and re-standardize the sum to obtain a continuous NSS7 score (mean ≈ 0; higher = greater neighborhood stress).
- Aggregate CBG-level NSS7 scores to tracts and counties using population-weighted means (ACS total population).

This NSS7 implementation is an independent, fully reproducible approximation based on the published methodology; it is not derived from the original MassHealth member-level data but is designed to be conceptually and numerically comparable to ReADI, NA-ADI, SDI, SVI, and FDep.

> FDep

We also include a French Deprivation Index (FDep)–style measure. FDep is a PCA-based deprivation index originally developed for France, combining four neighborhood-level indicators (income, education, blue-collar employment, and unemployment) [Rey et al. 2009](https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2458-9-33); [Temam et al. 2017](https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12889-017-4967-3).

In this analysis, we:

- Construct four ACS-based CBG-level variables analogous to the original FDep components (median household income, % high school graduates, % blue-collar workers, % unemployed).
- Standardize these variables and run principal components analysis (PCA).
- Use the **first principal component (PC1)** as the FDep score, orienting it so that higher values correspond to greater deprivation.
- Aggregate to tracts and counties using population-weighted means.

This yields a transparent PCA-based deprivation index in the FDep tradition that can be compared directly with ReADI, NA-ADI, SDI, SVI, and NSS7.

### Mortality 2010-2015
***

<br>

Census tract–level mortality data were obtained from the [U.S. Small-Area Life Expectancy Estimates Project (USALEEP)](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/usaleep/usaleep.html), which provides period life expectancy estimates for 2010–2015. We use tracts from the 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia and link them to our deprivation indices via the 11-digit census tract GEOID.

Tracts with missing or suppressed USALEEP estimates are excluded from all mortality analyses.

```{r, eval = F}
ADI_Mortality_Data$GEOID <- ADI_Mortality_Data$Tract.ID
stopifnot(all(nchar(ADI_Mortality_Data$GEOID) == 11),
 length(unique(ADI_Mortality_Data$GEOID)) == nrow(ADI_Mortality_Data))

ADI_Mortality_Data <- ADI_Mortality_Data[, c("GEOID", "e.0.")]
names(ADI_Mortality_Data)[names(ADI_Mortality_Data) == "e.0."] <- "Life_Expectancy"

common_geoids <- Reduce(intersect, list(ADI_Mortality_Data$GEOID, NA_ADI_CT_2015$GEOID, ReADI_CT_2015$GEOID))
ADI_Mortality_Data <- ADI_Mortality_Data[ADI_Mortality_Data$GEOID %in% common_geoids, ]

Pop_Total_2015$variable <- NULL
```

## Statistical Analysis
***

<br>

### ReADI and NA-ADI weights
***

<br>

ReADI variable weights come from the one-factor models fit in the ReADI 2022 creation script [ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd](https://github.com/ngladish/ReADI/blob/main/2018-2022/ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd). For each geography, we use psych::fa (principal factor method with population weights) and take the factor score coefficients ($weights), i.e., the linear weights applied to z-standardized census variables to generate the factor score. In this document we refer to these coefficients as the “ReADI weights.” 

To benchmark against the original ADI, we also attach Singh (2003)’s published factor score coefficients (the “Tract score coefficient” column in Table 1) to the same set of variables, storing them in the NA_ADI column of ReADI_2022_Wt. Thus:

- ReADI scores are the factor scores from our own models, rescaled to 0–100.

- NA-ADI weights are Singh’s published factor score coefficients, used only for comparing weight/loading patterns, not to recompute the official Neighborhood Atlas ADI.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code612">Show Code</button>

```{r, eval = F}
## 1. Defining the NA-ADI/Singh factor score coefficients
na_adi_weights <- c(
  MEDFI     = -0.0977,  # Median family income
  INCDIS    =  0.0936,  # Income disparity
  BELPL     =  0.0977,  # Families below poverty level
  PL150     =  0.1037,  # Population below 150% of poverty threshold
  EDU9YR    =  0.0849,  # < 9 years education
  HSDPNHIGH = -0.0970,  # ≥ high school diploma
  EMPWC     = -0.0874,  # White-collar employment
  UNEMP     =  0.0806,  # Unemployment
  MEDHV     = -0.0688,  # Median home value
  MEDRNT    = -0.0781,  # Median gross rent
  MEDMORT   = -0.0770,  # Median monthly mortgage
  OWN       = -0.0615,  # Owner-occupied housing
  SNGPNT    =  0.0719,  # Single-parent households
  NOVEH     =  0.0694,  # Households without a motor vehicle
  NOINT     =  0.0877,  # Households without a telephone/internet
  NOPLUM    =  0.0510,  # Units without complete plumbing (log)
  CROWD     =  0.0556   # >1 person per room
)

na_adi_df <- data.frame(Vars = names(na_adi_weights), NA_ADI = as.numeric(na_adi_weights), row.names = NULL)
ADI_2022_Wt <- merge(ReADI_2022_Wt, na_adi_df, by = "Vars", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
setdiff(na_adi_df$Vars, ADI_2022_Wt$Vars)   # should be character(0)
setdiff(ADI_2022_Wt$Vars, na_adi_df$Vars)   # anything here just won't get NA_ADI
```

### ReADI and NA-ADI loadings
***

<br>

ReADI variable loadings come from the one-factor models fit in the ReADI 2022 creation script [ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd](https://github.com/ngladish/ReADI/blob/main/2018-2022/ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd). For comparison with our ReADI weights and loadings, we also attach the original factor loadings reported by Singh (2003) for the 1990 census tract-level ADI. These loadings come directly from Table 1 of the Singh paper (column “Tract Loading”) and correspond to the same 17 component variables we use in ReADI (e.g., median family income, income disparity, % below poverty, % crowding, etc.).

In Singh’s work, these loadings describe the strength and direction of the association between each standardized census variable and the single latent deprivation factor. Kind et al. later reused the corresponding factor score coefficients (the weights) from this same 1990 tract model when constructing the Neighborhood Atlas ADI. Here, we explicitly separate:

ReADI weights/loadings, estimated de novo from contemporary ACS data, and

Singh (2003) tract loadings, taken verbatim from the original 1990 factor model.

We store the Singh tract loadings alongside the ReADI weights in ReADI_2022_Wt, aligned by variable name. This allows us to directly compare:
(i) ReADI vs Singh loadings, and
(ii) ReADI vs NA-ADI weights/loadings, using a consistent set of 17 harmonized variables.

### Combined ADI component dataset
***

<br>

For the 2018–2022 analyses, we construct a unified dataset that contains, for each geography, both ReADI and NA-ADI scores along with their underlying component variables. After harmonizing GEOIDs and restricting to areas with valid values for both indices, the analytic sample includes 235,952 census block groups (CBGs), 83,722 census tracts (CTs), and 3,214 counties with overlapping ReADI and NA-ADI scores.

The ReADI components (raw and standardized) and population weights come directly from the ReADI creation pipeline, as documented in [ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd](https://github.com/ngladish/ReADI/blob/main/2018-2022/ReADI_2022_Creation.Rmd).

The NA-ADI scores used here are the official national percentiles downloaded from the Neighborhood Atlas.

Because the Neighborhood Atlas does not release the underlying code or intermediate composite variables, we reconstructed NA-ADI–style components to enable indicator-level and methodological comparisons. These reverse-engineered NA-ADI components are described in detail in [RENA_2022.Rmd](https://github.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/RENA/RENA_2022.Rmd). Briefly, we implemented the published variable definitions, thresholds, and transformations from Singh (2003) and Kind et al. (2014), and aligned our approach with the independently developed replication by [Petterson; 2023](https://academic.oup.com/healthaffairsscholar/article/1/5/qxad063/7342005), who reported correlations >0.9999 between his reconstructed scores and the official NA-ADI.

In all analyses:

- Any NA-ADI score is the official Neighborhood Atlas value.

- Any NA-ADI component or raw indicator attributed to NA-ADI comes from this reverse-engineered implementation and should be interpreted as a high-fidelity approximation of the internal NA-ADI construction, not as an alternative version of the official index.

### Difference score calculation
***

<br>

To quantify how much the Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI) diverges from ReADI, we compute a simple difference score at each geography (CBG, tract, county):

Diff_NA_ReADI = NA_ADI − ReADI

Throughout, ReADI is treated as the reference implementation. Under this convention:
- Diff_NA_ReADI > 0 → NA-ADI assigns higher (more deprived) scores than ReADI (over-estimation of deprivation relative to ReADI).
- Diff_NA_ReADI < 0 → NA-ADI assigns lower (less deprived) scores than ReADI (under-estimation of deprivation relative to ReADI).

These difference scores are added to the CBG-, tract-, and county-level ADI datasets and are used in all subsequent analyses of agreement, bias, and urban–rural or regional patterns.

```{r}
load("ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")
load("ADI_C_Data.RData")
ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI <- ADI_CBG_Data$NA_ADI - ADI_CBG_Data$ReADI_CBG_NR
ADI_CT_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI <- ADI_CT_Data$NA_ADI - ADI_CT_Data$ReADI_CT_NR
ADI_C_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI <- ADI_C_Data$NA_ADI - ADI_C_Data$ReADI_C_NR
save(ADI_CBG_Data, file = "ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
save(ADI_CT_Data, file = "ADI_CT_Data.RData")
save(ADI_C_Data, file = "ADI_C_Data.RData")
```

### Difference correlation to components
***

<br>

```{r, eval = F}
load("ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")
load("ADI_C_Data.RData")

vars <- c("Diff_NA_ReADI", "MEDFI_Re", "INCDIS_Re", "BELPL_Re", "PL150_Re", "EDU9YR_Re", "HSDPNHIGH_Re", "EMPWC_Re", "UNEMP_Re", "MEDHV_Re", "MEDRNT_Re", "MEDMORT_Re", "OWN_Re", "SNGPNT_Re", "NOVEH_Re", "NOINT_Re", "NOPLUM_Re", "CROWD_Re")
var_names <- c("Median Family Income", "Income Disparity", "Below Poverty 100%", "Below Poverty 150%", "Low Education", "High Education", "White Collar Employment", "Unemployment", "Median Home Value", "Median Rent", "Median Mortgage", "Home Ownership", "Single Parent", "No Vehicle", "No Internet", "No Plumbing", "Crowded Housing")

make_diff_cor <- function(df, geo_label) {
  stopifnot(all(vars %in% colnames(df)))
  dat <- df[, vars]
  comp_vars <- vars[-1]
  cors <- sapply(comp_vars, function(v) {
    stats::cor(dat[["Diff_NA_ReADI"]], dat[[v]], use = "complete.obs")
  })
  pvals <- sapply(comp_vars, function(v) {
    stats::cor.test(dat[["Diff_NA_ReADI"]], dat[[v]], use = "complete.obs")$p.value
  })
  out <- data.frame(
    Vars      = comp_vars,
    Variables = var_names,
    Cor       = as.numeric(cors),
    P_value   = as.numeric(pvals),
    Geo       = geo_label,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  out}

ADI_Diff_Cor <- rbind(make_diff_cor(ADI_CBG_Data, "Block Group"), make_diff_cor(ADI_CT_Data,  "Census Tract"), make_diff_cor(ADI_C_Data,   "County"))

ADI_Diff_Cor <- ADI_Diff_Cor %>%
  group_by(Geo) %>%
  arrange(desc(Cor), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Ord = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

save(ADI_Diff_Cor, file = "ADI_Diff_Cor.RData")
```
  </div>
</div>

### Loading correlation dataset
***

<br>

To evaluate how closely each ADI’s empirical behavior matches its factor structure, we constructed a “loading–correlation” dataset that links, for every component and geography:

1. The Pearson correlation between the ADI score and each of the 17 component indicators; and  
2. The corresponding factor loading used to construct the index.

We do this separately for ReADI and NA-ADI and for each geography (census block group, census tract, and county), then stack the results into a single long-format dataset (`ADI_Cor_L`).

Concretely:
- We load the combined component datasets for ReADI and the reverse-engineered NA-ADI at each geography (`ADI_CBG_Data`, `ADI_CT_Data`, `ADI_C_Data`) and the table of Singh/Kind factor loadings (`ADI_2022_Loadings`).
- For each geography, we compute the correlation between the ADI score (ReADI or NA-ADI) and each standardized component.
- We strip the variable suffixes (`_Re`, `_NA`) to recover the common component names, then merge in the corresponding Singh/Kind loadings and ReADI loadings.
- Finally, we bind the block group, tract, and county results into a single dataset (`ADI_Cor_L`), which is used for the loading–correlation regressions and for Figure 2A (ReADI) and Figure 2B (NA-ADI) in the Results.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code821">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code821" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load("ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")
load("ADI_C_Data.RData")
load("ADI_2022_Loadings.RData")

NA_Vars <- c("MEDFI_NA", "INCDIS_NA", "BELPL_NA", "PL150_NA", "EDU9YR_NA", "HSDPNHIGH_NA", "EMPWC_NA", "UNEMP_NA", "MEDHV_NA", "MEDRNT_NA", "MEDMORT_NA", "OWN_NA", "SNGPNT_NA", "NOVEH_NA", "NOINT_NA", "NOPLUM_NA", "CROWD_NA")

Re_Vars <- c("MEDFI_Re", "INCDIS_Re", "BELPL_Re", "PL150_Re", "EDU9YR_Re", "HSDPNHIGH_Re", "EMPWC_Re", "UNEMP_Re", "MEDHV_Re", "MEDRNT_Re", "MEDMORT_Re", "OWN_Re", "SNGPNT_Re", "NOVEH_Re", "NOINT_Re", "NOPLUM_Re", "CROWD_Re")

Variables <- c("Median Family Income", "Income Disparity", "Below Poverty 100%", "Below Poverty 150%", "Low Education", "High Education", "White Collar Employment", "Unemployment", "Median Home Value", "Median Rent", "Median Mortgage", "Home Ownership", "Single Parent", "No Vehicle", "No Internet", "No Plumbing", "Crowded Housing")

build_cor_df <- function(dat, geo_label, na_target, re_target, na_vars, re_vars, var_labels, loadings_df) {
  ## NA-ADI correlations
  cor_na <- cor(dat[, c(na_target, na_vars)], use = "complete.obs")
  na_cor_vec <- cor_na[na_vars, na_target]

  ## ReADI correlations
  cor_re <- cor(dat[, c(re_target, re_vars)], use = "complete.obs")
  re_cor_vec <- cor_re[re_vars, re_target]
  base_na_names <- sub("_.*$", "", na_vars)
  base_re_names <- sub("_.*$", "", re_vars)

  stopifnot(
    identical(loadings_df$Vars, base_na_names),
    identical(base_na_names, base_re_names),
    length(var_labels) == length(base_na_names)
  )

  # Pick the right ReADI loading column for this geography
  re_col <- switch(
    geo_label,
    "CBG" = "CBG",
    "CT"  = "CT",
    "C"   = "C",
    stop("Unknown geo_label: ", geo_label)
  )

  data.frame(
    Vars            = base_na_names,
    Variables       = var_labels,
    Geo             = geo_label,
    NA_Cor          = as.numeric(na_cor_vec),
    ReADI_Cor       = as.numeric(re_cor_vec),
    NA_ADI_Loadings = loadings_df$NA_ADI,     # Singh / NA-ADI weights (same across geos)
    ReADI_Loadings  = loadings_df[[re_col]],  # ReADI weights for this geography
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Build for each geography ------------------------------------------------------

ADI_Cor_CBG <- build_cor_df(dat = ADI_CBG_Data, geo_label = "CBG", na_target = "NA_ADI", re_target = "ReADI_CBG_NR", na_vars = NA_Vars, re_vars = Re_Vars, var_labels = Variables, loadings_df = ADI_2022_Loadings)

ADI_Cor_CT <- build_cor_df(dat        = ADI_CT_Data,geo_label  = "CT",na_target  = "NA_ADI",re_target  = "ReADI_CT_NR", na_vars    = NA_Vars, re_vars    = Re_Vars, var_labels = Variables, loadings_df = ADI_2022_Loadings)

ADI_Cor_C <- build_cor_df(dat        = ADI_C_Data, geo_label  = "C", na_target  = "NA_ADI", re_target  = "ReADI_C_NR", na_vars    = NA_Vars, re_vars    = Re_Vars, var_labels = Variables, loadings_df = ADI_2022_Loadings)

# Combine and save --------------------------------------------------------------

ADI_Cor_L <- rbind(ADI_Cor_CBG, ADI_Cor_CT, ADI_Cor_C)
ADI_Cor_L$Geography <- ifelse(ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", "Block Group", ADI_Cor_L$Geo)
ADI_Cor_L$Geography <- ifelse(ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CT", "Census Tract", ADI_Cor_L$Geography)
ADI_Cor_L$Geography <- ifelse(ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "C", "County", ADI_Cor_L$Geography)
save(ADI_Cor_L, file = "ADI_Cor_L.RData")
```
  </div>
</div>

### Urban–rural and regional designation
***

<br>

To evaluate potential urban–rural bias in ReADI and NA-ADI, we assign an urban/rural flag to census tracts and block groups using the 2020 Census Urban Area (UAC10) shapefile from the TIGER/Line database (downloaded directly from the U.S. Census Bureau). After harmonizing coordinate reference systems, each tract and block group polygon is intersected with the UAC10 polygons: any unit that overlaps a designated urban area is labeled Urban, and all others are labeled Rural.

We then attach state FIPS, state name, and Census region (Midwest, Northeast, South, West; including the District of Columbia in the South) using the tigris::fips_codes crosswalk. Geometry is dropped and these labels are merged into the analysis datasets (ADI_CBG_Data and ADI_CT_Data), so downstream models can use urban/rural and region without needing spatial objects.

We do not classify counties as urban or rural. Although ReADI is calculated at the county level for policy interpretation and linkage to county-level health data, counties typically contain a mix of urban and rural tracts, making a binary county label misleading. All formal urban–rural bias analyses are therefore conducted at the census tract level, with block groups used descriptively.

Using this approach we identify:

- Census block groups (n = 240,165): 30,318 rural and 209,847 urban
  - Midwest: 55,119 total (9,662 rural; 45,457 urban)
  - Northeast: 43,456 total (3,677 rural; 39,779 urban)
  - South: 86,845 total (13,412 rural; 73,433 urban)
  - West: 52,255 total (3,548 rural; 48,707 urban)
  
- Census tracts (n = 84,535): 8,410 rural and 76,125 urban
  - Midwest: 18,421 total (2,487 rural; 15,934 urban)
  - Northeast: 14,551 total (994 rural; 13,557 urban)
  - South: 31,995 total (3,878 rural; 28,117 urban)
  - West: 18,646 total (1,049 rural; 17,597 urban)

These final urban–rural and region labels are stored in ADI_CBG_Data and ADI_CT_Data and used in all subsequent stratified and bias analyses.

```{r, eval = F}
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry.RData"))
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/ACS_CT_2022_Geometry.RData"))
load("ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")

## Download and read Census 2020 urban area shapefile --------------------------
temp_dir <- tempdir()
zip_url <- "https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2020/UAC/tl_2020_us_uac10.zip"
zip_file <- file.path(temp_dir, "urban_areas.zip")

resp <- httr::GET(zip_url, write_disk(zip_file, overwrite = TRUE))
stopifnot(httr::status_code(resp) == 200)
unzip(zip_file, exdir = temp_dir)

shp_file <- list.files(temp_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(shp_file) == 1L)   # should only be the UAC shapefile
urban_areas <- sf::st_read(shp_file, quiet = TRUE)

## Align CRS ------------------------------------------------------------------

if (sf::st_crs(urban_areas) != sf::st_crs(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry)) {
  urban_areas <- sf::st_transform(urban_areas, sf::st_crs(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry))}

if (sf::st_crs(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry) != sf::st_crs(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry)) {
  ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry <- sf::st_transform(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry, sf::st_crs(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry))}

## Add urban/rural flag ---------------------------------------------

add_urban_label <- function(sf_obj, urban_sf) {
  hits <- sf::st_intersects(sf_obj, urban_sf)
  sf_obj$urban_label <- factor(
    ifelse(lengths(hits) > 0, "Urban", "Rural"),
    levels = c("Rural", "Urban"))
   sf_obj}

ACS_CT_2022_Geometry  <- add_urban_label(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry,  urban_areas)
ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry <- add_urban_label(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry, urban_areas)

## Adding regions --------------------------------------------------------

fips_crosswalk <- fips_codes %>%
  distinct(state_code, state_name, state) %>%        # state = USPS abbrev
  filter(state %in% c(state.abb, "DC")) %>%          # include DC explicitly
  mutate(region_raw = case_when(state == "DC" ~ "South",            
      TRUE ~ state.region[match(state, state.abb)]),
    region = dplyr::recode(region_raw, "North Central" = "Midwest")) %>%
  transmute(
    STATEFP    = state_code,
    state_name = state_name,
    region     = region)

## Tracts
ACS_CT_2022_Geometry <- ACS_CT_2022_Geometry %>%
  mutate(STATEFP = substr(GEOID, 1, 2)) %>%
  left_join(fips_crosswalk, by = "STATEFP")

## Block groups
ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry <- ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry %>%
  mutate(STATEFP = substr(GEOID, 1, 2)) %>%
  left_join(fips_crosswalk, by = "STATEFP")

## Quick sanity checks --------------------------------------------------------

table(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry$urban_label)
table(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry$urban_label)
table(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry$region)
table(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry$region)
table(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry$region, ACS_CT_2022_Geometry$urban_label)
table(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry$region, ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry$urban_label)

## Combining with ADI data --------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(anyDuplicated(ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry$GEOID) == 0, anyDuplicated(ADI_CBG_Data$GEOID) == 0, anyDuplicated(ACS_CT_2022_Geometry$GEOID) == 0, anyDuplicated(ADI_CT_Data$GEOID) == 0)

ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry <- ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% select(GEOID, STATEFP, state_name, urban_label, region)
ADI_CBG_Data <- plyr::join(ADI_CBG_Data, ACS_CBG_2022_Geometry, by   = "GEOID", type = "left")

ACS_CT_2022_Geometry <- ACS_CT_2022_Geometry %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% select(GEOID, STATEFP, state_name, urban_label, region)
ADI_CT_Data <- plyr::join(ADI_CT_Data, ACS_CT_2022_Geometry, by   = "GEOID", type = "left")

## Regional/urban summaries --------------------------------------------------------

CT_region_summary <- ADI_CT_Data %>%
  group_by(state_name, region, urban_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_diff = mean(Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_diff = sd(Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tracts = n(),
    se_diff = sd_diff / sqrt(n_tracts),
    .groups = "drop")
CT_region_summary <- CT_region_summary[!is.na(CT_region_summary$state_name),]

CBG_region_summary <- ADI_CBG_Data %>%
  group_by(state_name, region, urban_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_diff = mean(Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_diff = sd(Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cbgs = n(),
    se_diff = sd_diff / sqrt(n_cbgs),
    .groups = "drop")
CBG_region_summary <- CBG_region_summary[!is.na(CBG_region_summary$state_name),]

## Saving objects --------------------------------------------------------
save(ADI_CBG_Data, file = "ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
save(ADI_CT_Data, file = "ADI_CT_Data.RData")
save(CBG_region_summary, file = "CBG_region_summary.RData")
save(CT_region_summary, file = "CT_region_summary.RData")
```

# Results
***
<br>

We structured the analyses to evaluate how closely the Reproducible Area Deprivation Index (ReADI) recapitulates the Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI), where and why the two indices diverge, and whether those divergences matter for downstream applications such as comparisons with other indices and prediction of mortality.

We first assess agreement between NA-ADI and ReADI scores and factor loadings across block group, tract, and county geographies, and compare how each index aligns with other widely used deprivation and vulnerability measures (SDI, SVI, FDep, NSS7). We then quantify where NA-ADI and ReADI differ most in absolute score terms and how those discrepancies are distributed across the U.S. and by urban–rural status. Finally, we examine whether ReADI’s differences from NA-ADI translate into gains in explained variance for 2015 life expectancy, overall and within bins defined by the magnitude of NA-ADI vs ReADI disagreement.

## Agreement between ADI scores (linear regression)

To quantify agreement between the Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI) and the Reproducible ADI (ReADI) at each geographic level, we restricted the data to block groups, tracts, and counties with non-missing scores on both indices and:

- created analysis datasets containing only NA-ADI, ReADI, and a geography label (`Block Group`, `Census Tract`, `County`), dropping rows with missing values using `complete.cases()`;  
- fit simple linear regressions of ReADI on NA-ADI separately for each geography, extracted R-squared as a summary of agreement, and used `MBESS::ci.R2()` to obtain 95% confidence intervals for R-squared; and  
- computed the RMSE between NA-ADI and ReADI for each geography, using the squared differences (`Diff_NA_ReADI`) and a delta-method approximation to derive a standard error, and constructed 95% confidence intervals as RMSE ± 1.96 × SE.

The printed outputs from this chunk reproduce the R-squared ranges and RMSE values (with 95% confidence intervals) reported in the Results section and provide the summary statistics underlying Figure 1A.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code1114">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code1114" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load("ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")
load("ADI_C_Data.RData")

ADI_CBG <- ADI_CBG_Data[, c("ReADI_CBG_NR", "NA_ADI")]
ADI_CBG <- ADI_CBG[complete.cases(ADI_CBG),]
ADI_CBG$Geography <- "Block Group"
colnames(ADI_CBG) <- c("ReADI", "NA_ADI", "Geography")
ADI_CT <- ADI_CT_Data[, c("ReADI_CT_NR", "NA_ADI")]
ADI_CT <- ADI_CT[complete.cases(ADI_CT),]
ADI_CT$Geography <- "Census Tract"
colnames(ADI_CT) <- c("ReADI", "NA_ADI", "Geography")
ADI_C <- ADI_C_Data[, c("ReADI_C_NR", "NA_ADI")]
ADI_C <- ADI_C[complete.cases(ADI_C),]
ADI_C$Geography <- "County"
colnames(ADI_C) <- c("ReADI", "NA_ADI", "Geography")

# Ns
nrow(ADI_CBG)
nrow(ADI_CT)
nrow(ADI_C)

# linear regression
r2 <- summary(lm(ADI_CBG_Data$ReADI_CBG_NR ~ ADI_CBG_Data$NA_ADI))$r.squared
ciu <- ci.R2(R2 = summary(lm(ReADI_CBG_NR ~ NA_ADI, data = ADI_CBG_Data))$r.squared, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_CBG_Data) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)[[1]]
cil <- ci.R2(R2 = summary(lm(ReADI_CBG_NR ~ NA_ADI, data = ADI_CBG_Data))$r.squared, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_CBG_Data) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)[[3]]
paste(round(r2, 3), " (95% CI, ", round(ciu, 3), "-", round(cil, 3), ")", sep="")

r2 <- summary(lm(ADI_CT_Data$ReADI_CT_NR ~ ADI_CT_Data$NA_ADI))$r.squared
ciu <- ci.R2(R2 = summary(lm(ReADI_CT_NR ~ NA_ADI, data = ADI_CT_Data))$r.squared, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_CT_Data) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)[[1]]
cil <- ci.R2(R2 = summary(lm(ReADI_CT_NR ~ NA_ADI, data = ADI_CT_Data))$r.squared, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_CT_Data) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)[[3]]
paste(round(r2, 3), " (95% CI, ", round(ciu, 3), "-", round(cil, 3), ")", sep="")

r2 <- summary(lm(ADI_C_Data$ReADI_C_NR ~ ADI_C_Data$NA_ADI))$r.squared
ciu <- ci.R2(R2 = summary(lm(ReADI_C_NR ~ NA_ADI, data = ADI_C_Data))$r.squared, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_C_Data) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)[[1]]
cil <- ci.R2(R2 = summary(lm(ReADI_C_NR ~ NA_ADI, data = ADI_C_Data))$r.squared, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_C_Data) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)[[3]]
paste(round(r2, 3), " (95% CI, ", round(ciu, 3), "-", round(cil, 3), ")", sep="")

# rmse
ADI_CBG_Data <- ADI_CBG_Data[!is.na(ADI_CBG_Data$NA_ADI),]
rmse_obs <- Metrics::rmse(ADI_CBG_Data$ReADI_CBG_NR, ADI_CBG_Data$NA_ADI)
se_rmse <- sd((ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI)^2) / (2 * rmse_obs * sqrt(length(ADI_CBG_Data$ReADI_CBG_NR)))
ci <- rmse_obs + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se_rmse
paste(round(rmse_obs, 1), " (95% CI, ", round(ci[1], 1), "-", round(ci[2], 1), ")", sep = "")

ADI_CT_Data <- ADI_CT_Data[!is.na(ADI_CT_Data$NA_ADI),]
rmse_obs <- Metrics::rmse(ADI_CT_Data$ReADI_CT_NR, ADI_CT_Data$NA_ADI)
se_rmse <- sd((ADI_CT_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI)^2) / (2 * rmse_obs * sqrt(length(ADI_CT_Data$ReADI_CT_NR)))
ci <- rmse_obs + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se_rmse
paste(round(rmse_obs, 1), " (95% CI, ", round(ci[1], 1), "-", round(ci[2], 1), ")", sep = "")

ADI_C_Data <- ADI_C_Data[!is.na(ADI_C_Data$NA_ADI),]
rmse_obs <- Metrics::rmse(ADI_C_Data$ReADI_C_NR, ADI_C_Data$NA_ADI)
se_rmse <- sd((ADI_C_Data$ReADI_C_NR - ADI_C_Data$NA_ADI)^2) / (2 * rmse_obs * sqrt(length(ADI_C_Data$ReADI_C_NR)))
ci <- rmse_obs + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se_rmse
paste(round(rmse_obs, 1), " (95% CI, ", round(ci[1], 1), "-", round(ci[2], 1), ")", sep = "")
```

## Figure 1A
***
> Figure 1. Comparison of Neighborhood Atlas Area Deprivation Index (NA-ADI) and Reproducible ADI (ReADI) Scores and Factor Weights at Multiple Geographic Scales. A. Associations between the NA-ADI and ReADI scores.

This figure visualizes the relationship between the Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI) and the Reproducible ADI (ReADI) across geographic levels. Using the cleaned datasets (`ADI_CBG`, `ADI_CT`, `ADI_C`), we stack block group, tract, and county data into a single long-format object (`ADI_Merge`) with a `Geography` indicator, plot ReADI (x-axis) versus NA-ADI (y-axis) as scatterplots, overlay linear fits with `geom_smooth(method = "lm")`, and use `facet_wrap(~Geography)` to produce separate panels for block groups, census tracts, and counties on a comparable scale.

This reproduces Figure 1A in the manuscript, showing how closely NA-ADI tracks ReADI at each geographic scale and providing the visual counterpart to the R² and RMSE summaries reported above.

```{r, eval = F}
ADI_Merge <- rbind(ADI_Merge, ADI_C)
ggplot(ADI_Merge, aes(ReADI, NA_ADI, group = Geography)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#0D5F79", size = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', color = "darkgrey") +
  ylab("Neighborhood Atlas ADI") +
  xlab("Reproducible ADI") +
  facet_wrap(~Geography) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18)
```

## Agreement between ADI factor loadings (linear regression)

This panel compares the factor loadings (weights) assigned to each socioeconomic indicator in NA-ADI and ReADI across geographic levels. The data frame `ADI_2022_Wt` contains, for each indicator, the original NA-ADI weight (from the Singh tract-level formulation) and the corresponding ReADI weights at the block group (`CBG`), census tract (`CT`), and county (`C`) levels.

We assign descriptive labels to indicators (e.g., income, education, employment, housing), reshape the weights to long format (`sub`) so each row represents an indicator–geography pair, and plot ReADI weights on the x-axis against NA-ADI weights on the y-axis, with points colored by indicator (`Variables`). A linear fit is overlaid in each panel, and `facet_wrap(~Geography)` produces separate panels for block groups, tracts, and counties.

This figure corresponds to Figure 1B in the manuscript and visually summarizes how closely the ReADI factor loadings reproduce the original NA-ADI weights across indicators and geographies.

```{r}
## Linear regression

ci <- ci.R2(R2 = r2, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_2022_Wt) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)

round(range(ADI_2022_Wt$CBG, ADI_2022_Wt$CT, ADI_2022_Wt$C), 3)
```

### Figure 1B

> Figure 1. Comparison of Neighborhood Atlas Area Deprivation Index (NA-ADI) and Reproducible ADI (ReADI) Scores and Factor Weights at Multiple Geographic Scales. B. Factor weights of economic indicators.

This panel compares the factor loadings (weights) assigned to each socioeconomic indicator in NA-ADI versus ReADI across geographic levels. The data frame `ADI_2022_Wt` contains, for each indicator, the original NA-ADI weight (derived from the Singh tract-level formulation) and the corresponding ReADI weights at the block group (`CBG`), census tract (`CT`), and county (`C`) levels. We:

- Assign a descriptive label to each indicator (for example, median family income, income disparity, below-poverty thresholds, unemployment, housing characteristics).  
- Reshape the weight data into long format (`sub`), with one row per indicator–geography combination and a variable indicating geography (block group, census tract, county).  
- Plot ReADI weights on the x-axis and NA-ADI weights on the y-axis, with each point representing one indicator. Points are colored by indicator (`Variables`) and a linear fit is overlaid within each panel.  
- Use `facet_wrap(~Geography)` so that separate panels show the weight relationships at the block group, tract, and county levels.

This figure corresponds to Figure 1B in the manuscript and visually summarizes how closely the ReADI factor loadings reproduce the original NA-ADI weights across indicators and geographies.

## Comparison of correlation between ADI score and indicator with the factor loading of that indicator

In this section we assess whether indicators that are more strongly associated with the ADI scores are also given larger factor loadings, and how this relationship compares between ReADI and NA-ADI across geographic levels. The data frame `ADI_Cor_L` contains, for each indicator and geography (block group, tract, county), the ReADI–indicator correlation (`ReADI_Cor`), the NA-ADI–indicator correlation (`NA_Cor`), the corresponding ReADI loading (`ReADI_Loadings`), the NA-ADI loading (`NA_ADI_Loadings`), and a geography label (`Geo` = "CBG", "CT", "C").

We summarize this relationship separately for ReADI and NA-ADI:

- **ReADI**  
  - For each geography, fit a simple linear regression of `ReADI_Cor` on `ReADI_Loadings` and extract the R-squared as a measure of how well the ReADI weights explain the pattern of indicator correlations, obtaining 95% CIs with `MBESS::ci.R2()`.  
  - Compute the RMSE between `ReADI_Cor` and `ReADI_Loadings` using `Metrics::rmse()`, and use `boot::boot()` with 2,000 resamples and `boot.ci(type = "perc")` to obtain bootstrap 95% CIs for the RMSE.  
  - Summarize the minimum and maximum R-squared and RMSE values (with CIs) across geographies and generate per-geography “R² = … (RMSE, …)” labels used to annotate the ReADI panels.

- **NA-ADI**  
  - Repeat the same analyses using `NA_Cor` and `NA_ADI_Loadings`, fitting regressions of `NA_Cor` on `NA_ADI_Loadings`, extracting R-squared and CIs, and computing RMSE and bootstrap CIs.  
  - Summarize ranges across geographies and generate the analogous “R² (RMSE)” labels for the NA-ADI panels.

The printed output from this chunk provides the R-squared and RMSE ranges (with 95% confidence intervals) reported in the Results and the per-geography R-squared/RMSE values displayed alongside the ReADI (Figure 2A) and NA-ADI (Figure 2B) panels.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code1325">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code1325" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load("ADI_Cor_L.RData")

### ReADI
#### Linear regression
r2_cbg <- summary(lm(ReADI_Cor ~ ReADI_Loadings, data = ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", ]))$r.squared
ci_cbg <- ci.R2(R2 = r2_cbg, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", ]) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)
r2_ct <- summary(lm(ReADI_Cor ~ ReADI_Loadings, data = ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CT", ]))$r.squared
ci_ct <- ci.R2(R2 = r2_ct, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CT", ]) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)
r2_c <- summary(lm(ReADI_Cor ~ ReADI_Loadings, data = ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "C", ]))$r.squared
ci_c <- ci.R2(R2 = r2_c, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "C", ]) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)
r2 <- min(r2_cbg, r2_ct, r2_c)
cil <- min(ci_cbg[[1]], ci_ct[[1]], ci_c[[1]])
ciu <- max(ci_cbg[[3]], ci_ct[[3]], ci_c[[3]])
paste("R^2 ≥ ", round(r2,3), " [95% CI, ", round(cil, 3), "-", round(ciu,3), "]", sep = "")

#### RMSE
rmse_stat <- function(data, indices) {
  d <- data[indices, ]
  Metrics::rmse(d$ReADI_Cor, d$ReADI_Loadings)}
sub <- ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", ]
rmse_cbg <- Metrics::rmse(sub$ReADI_Cor, sub$ReADI_Loadings)
set.seed(2374)
b <- boot(sub, statistic = rmse_stat, R = 2000)
ci_cbg <- boot.ci(b, type = c("perc"))$percent
sub <- ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CT", ]
rmse_ct <- Metrics::rmse(sub$ReADI_Cor, sub$ReADI_Loadings)
set.seed(2374)
b <- boot(sub, statistic = rmse_stat, R = 2000)
ci_ct <- boot.ci(b, type = c("perc"))$percent
sub <- ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "C", ]
rmse_c <- Metrics::rmse(sub$ReADI_Cor, sub$ReADI_Loadings)
set.seed(2374)
b <- boot(sub, statistic = rmse_stat, R = 2000)
ci_c <- boot.ci(b, type = c("perc"))$percent

rsme <- min(rmse_cbg, rmse_ct, rmse_c)
cil <- min(ci_cbg[4], ci_ct[4], ci_c[4])
ciu <- min(ci_cbg[5], ci_ct[5], ci_c[5])
paste(round(rsme,3), " [95% CI, ", round(cil, 3), "-", round(ciu, 3), "]", sep = "")

rsme <- max(rmse_cbg, rmse_ct, rmse_c)
cil <- max(ci_cbg[4], ci_ct[4], ci_c[4])
ciu <- max(ci_cbg[5], ci_ct[5], ci_c[5])
paste(round(rsme,3), " [95% CI, ", round(cil, 3), "-", round(ciu, 3), "]", sep = "")

## For Figure 2A:
paste("R^2 = ", round(r2_cbg,3), " (RMSE, ", round(rmse_cbg, 3), ")", sep = "")
paste("R^2 = ", round(r2_ct,3), " (RMSE, ", round(rmse_ct, 3), ")", sep = "")
paste("R^2 = ", round(r2_c,3), " (RMSE, ", round(rmse_c, 3), ")", sep = "")

### NA-ADI
#### Linear regression
r2_cbg <- summary(lm(NA_Cor ~ NA_ADI_Loadings, data = ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", ]))$r.squared
ci_cbg <- ci.R2(R2 = r2_cbg, df.1 = 1, df.2 = nrow(ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", ]) - 1 - 1, conf.level = 0.95)
r2_ct <- summary(lm(NA_Cor ~ NA_ADI_Loadings, data = ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CT", ]))$r.squared

r2 <- min(r2_cbg, r2_ct, r2_c)
cil <- min(ci_cbg[[1]], ci_ct[[1]], ci_c[[1]])
ciu <- min(ci_cbg[[3]], ci_ct[[3]], ci_c[[3]])

ciu <- max(ci_cbg[[3]], ci_ct[[3]], ci_c[[3]])
paste(round(r2, 3), " [95% CI, ", round(cil, 3), "-", round(ciu, 3), "]", sep = "")

#### RMSE 
rmse_stat <- function(data, indices) {
  d <- data[indices, ]

sub <- ADI_Cor_L[ADI_Cor_L$Geo == "CBG", ]
```

### Figure 2A (ReADI) & 2B (NA-ADI)

> Figure 2. Consistency Between Area Deprivation Index (ADI) Component Correlations and Factor Loadings Across Geographic Levels. A. ReADI scores. B. NA-ADI scores.

These panels show, for each ADI component and geography, the correlation of that component with the ADI score alongside its factor loading, to visually assess how well the weighting scheme aligns with how strongly each indicator relates to the score.

Using the long-format `ADI_Cor_L` object, we:
- select, for each geography (block group, census tract, county), the indicator name (`Variables`), geography (`Geography`), and either  
  - ReADI correlations and loadings (`ReADI_Cor`, `ReADI_Loadings`) for Figure 2A, or  
  - NA-ADI correlations and loadings (`NA_Cor`, `NA_ADI_Loadings`) for Figure 2B;
- convert `Variables` to a factor and order indicators by their correlation with the corresponding ADI score at the block group level, then carry this ordering across all geographies so indicators appear in a consistent order; and  
- reshape to long format and plot side-by-side bars (correlation vs loading) for each indicator using `facet_wrap(~Geography)` and `coord_flip()` for readability.

Figure 2A shows ReADI correlations versus ReADI loadings; Figure 2B shows NA-ADI correlations versus the original Singh loadings. The per-panel R² and RMSE values and their bootstrap confidence intervals are computed in the preceding chunk and used to annotate the manuscript figures.

## Correlation of ADIs with SDI, SVI, FDep, and NSS7

Here we compare ReADI and NA-ADI to several widely used deprivation and vulnerability indices across geographic levels:

- Social Deprivation Index (SDI)  
- Social Vulnerability Index (SVI)  
- French Deprivation Index (FDep)  
- Neighborhood Stress Score (NSS7)

For each geography (block group, census tract, county), we:

- merge the ADI datasets (`ADI_CBG_Data`, `ADI_CT_Data`, `ADI_C_Data`) with the corresponding SDVI datasets (`SDVI_CBG_2022`, `SDVI_CT_2022`, `SDVI_C_2022`) by `GEOID`, keeping ReADI deciles (`ReADI_xtile`), NA-ADI (`NA_ADI`), FDep, SDI, SVI, and NSS7, and relabel the columns to a common set of names (`sdvi_names`);  
- restrict to complete cases and compute Pearson correlation matrices among the six indices, using a helper (`cor_mtest`) to obtain 95% confidence intervals and storing, for each geography, matrices of correlations (`cor`) and lower/upper CI bounds (`cil`, `ciu`); and  
- extract, for ReADI and NA-ADI in turn, the correlations (and CI bounds) with the other indices (excluding the correlation between ReADI and NA-ADI itself) and use `range_across_geos()` to obtain the minimum and maximum correlations and corresponding 95% CI bounds across CBG, CT, and C.

The printed outputs give the minimum and maximum correlations (with 95% CIs) for ReADI and NA-ADI versus SDI, SVI, FDep, and NSS7 across geographies, corresponding to the correlation ranges reported in the Results.

<div style="margin:16px 0">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-dark" control-id="ControlID-54" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#code1571">Show Code</button>
  <div id="code1571" class="collapse">
```{r, eval = F}
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/Other_Indices/SDVI_CBG_2022.RData"))
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/Other_Indices/SDVI_CT_2022.RData"))
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ngladish/Publications/main/Gladish_2025_ReADI_Creation/Other_Indices/SDVI_C_2022.RData"))
load("ADI_CBG_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")
load("ADI_C_Data.RData")

sdvi_names <- c("Reproducible\nADI", "Neighborhood\n Atlas ADI", "French\nDeprivation Index", "Social\nDeprivation Index", "Social\nVulnerability Index", "Neighborhood\nStress Score")

CBG <- ADI_CBG_Data[, c("GEOID", "ReADI_CBG_NR", "NA_ADI")]
SDVI_CBG_2022 <- SDVI_CBG_2022[, c("GEOID", "FDep", "SDI", "SVI", "NSS7")]
CBG <- plyr::join(CBG, SDVI_CBG_2022, by = "GEOID", type = "left")
CBG$GEOID <- NULL
colnames(CBG) <- sdvi_names

CT <- ADI_CT_Data[, c("GEOID", "ReADI_CT_NR", "NA_ADI")]
SDVI_CT_2022 <- SDVI_CT_2022[, c("GEOID", "FDep", "SDI", "SVI", "NSS7")]
CT <- plyr::join(CT, SDVI_CT_2022, by = "GEOID", type = "left")
CT$GEOID <- NULL
colnames(CT) <- sdvi_names

C <- ADI_C_Data[, c("GEOID", "ReADI_C_NR", "NA_ADI")]
SDVI_C_2022 <- SDVI_C_2022[, c("GEOID", "FDep", "SDI", "SVI", "NSS7")]
C <- plyr::join(C, SDVI_C_2022, by = "GEOID", type = "left")
C$GEOID <- NULL
colnames(C) <- sdvi_names

# Stats
drop_naadi  <- "Neighborhood\n Atlas ADI"
drop_readi  <- "Reproducible\nADI"

# correlation or CI matrix with diagonal NA
cor_ci_mat <- function(df, what = c("cor", "lowCI", "uppCI")) {
  what  <- match.arg(what)
  df_cc <- df[complete.cases(df), ]
  if (what == "cor") {
    m <- cor(df_cc)} else {
    ci <- cor.mtest(df_cc)
    m  <- ci[[what]]
  }
  diag(m) <- NA
  as.data.frame(m)
}
# drop a given index from rows/cols
drop_index <- function(m, idx_label) {
  m[!rownames(m) %in% idx_label,
    !colnames(m) %in% idx_label]
}
# get min/max across CBG/CT/C for a given column and matrix type
range_across_geos <- function(mats, which_mat, col, drop_label) {
  vals <- sapply(mats, function(x) {
    drop_index(x[[which_mat]], drop_label)[[col]]
  })
  c(min = min(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(vals, na.rm = TRUE))
}
CBG_stats <- list(cor = cor_ci_mat(CBG, what = "cor"), cil = cor_ci_mat(CBG, what = "lowCI"), ciu = cor_ci_mat(CBG, what = "uppCI"))
CT_stats <- list(cor = cor_ci_mat(CT, what = "cor"), cil = cor_ci_mat(CT, what = "lowCI"), ciu = cor_ci_mat(CT, what = "uppCI"))
C_stats <- list(cor = cor_ci_mat(C, what = "cor"), cil = cor_ci_mat(C, what = "lowCI"), ciu = cor_ci_mat(C, what = "uppCI"))
all_stats <- list(CBG = CBG_stats, CT = CT_stats, C = C_stats)

re_cor <- range_across_geos(all_stats, "cor", col = "Reproducible\nADI", drop_label = drop_naadi)
re_cil <- range_across_geos(all_stats, "cil", col = "Reproducible\nADI", drop_label = drop_naadi)
re_ciu <- range_across_geos(all_stats, "ciu", col = "Reproducible\nADI", drop_label = drop_naadi)
paste(round(re_cor["min"], 3), " (95% CI, ", round(re_cil["min"], 3), "-", round(re_ciu["min"], 3), ")", sep = "")
paste(round(re_cor["max"], 3), " (95% CI, ", round(re_cil["max"], 3), "-", round(re_ciu["max"], 3), ")", sep = "")

na_cor <- range_across_geos(all_stats, "cor", col = "Neighborhood\n Atlas ADI", drop_label = drop_readi)
na_cil <- range_across_geos(all_stats, "cil", col = "Neighborhood\n Atlas ADI", drop_label = drop_readi)
na_ciu <- range_across_geos(all_stats, "ciu", col = "Neighborhood\n Atlas ADI", drop_label = drop_readi)

paste(round(na_cor["min"], 3), " (95% CI, ", round(na_cil["min"], 3), "-", round(na_ciu["min"], 3), ")", sep = "")
paste(round(na_cor["max"], 3), " (95% CI, ", round(na_cil["max"], 3), "-", round(na_ciu["max"], 3), ")", sep = "")
```

### Figure 3

> Figure 3. Pearson Correlations Between the Reproducible Area Deprivation Index (ReADI) and Neighborhood Atlas ADI (NA-ADI) and the 3 Established Deprivation Indices Across Geographic Levels A. Block Group. B. Census Tract. C. County.

This figure shows the correlation structure among ReADI, NA-ADI, and four other area-based indices (SDI, SVI, FDep, NSS7) at each geographic level. Using the `CBG`, `CT`, and `C` datasets (block groups, tracts, counties), we restrict to complete cases, compute Pearson correlation matrices for the six indices, and plot the upper triangle of each matrix with `corrplot()`. Rows and columns are ordered by the first principal component (`order = "FPC"`) so indices with similar correlation patterns cluster together, and we apply a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold (`sig.level = 0.05/15`) using p-values from `cor.mtest()`. Numeric correlation coefficients are overlaid and each panel is labeled “Block Group,” “Census Tract,” or “County”.

The resulting three-panel plot reproduces Figure 3 in the manuscript and illustrates how consistently ReADI and NA-ADI align with SDI, SVI, FDep, and NSS7 across block group, tract, and county geographies.

## Distribution of the difference between the ReADI from the NA-ADI

Here we summarize how much NA-ADI and ReADI differ numerically at each geographic level. In `ADI_CBG_Data`, `ADI_CT_Data`, and `ADI_C_Data`, the variable `Diff_NA_ReADI` gives the difference between NA-ADI and ReADI for each unit (on the 0–100 ADI scale).

For each geography (block group, tract, county), we:
- compute the range (minimum to maximum) and standard deviation of `Diff_NA_ReADI` among non-missing observations, and print these as “min to max (SD, sd_value)” to describe how far the indices can diverge; and  
- count how many units have an absolute difference of at least 20 points (`Diff_NA_ReADI <= -20` or `>= 20`), and report this as “X of N units (Y%)”, corresponding to the “discrepancies of 20 points or greater” statistics in the Results.

The geometry object `ACS_C_2022_Geometry.RData` is loaded here in preparation for later county-level maps of these differences, but is not used directly in this summary chunk.

```{r, eval = F}
load("ADI_C_Data.RData")
load("ADI_CT_Data.RData")

# Stats
## Range of difference by geography
range <- range(ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = T)
sd <- sd(ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = T)
paste(round(range[1], 1), " to ", round(range[2], 1), " (SD, ", round(sd, 1), ")", sep = "")

range <- range(ADI_CT_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = T)
sd <- sd(ADI_CT_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = T)
paste(round(range[1], 1), " to ", round(range[2], 1), " (SD, ", round(sd, 1), ")", sep = "")

range <- range(ADI_C_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = T)
sd <- sd(ADI_C_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI, na.rm = T)
paste(round(range[1], 1), " to ", round(range[2], 1), " (SD, ", round(sd, 1), ")", sep = "")

## Amount different by 20 points by geo
ADI_CBG_Data <- ADI_CBG_Data[!is.na(ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI),]
disc_20 <- sum(ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI <= -20 | ADI_CBG_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI >= 20, na.rm = T)

ADI_CT_Data <- ADI_CT_Data[!is.na(ADI_CT_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI),]

paste(round(disc_20, 1), " of ", round(nrow(ADI_CT_Data), 1), " (", round(100*(disc_20/nrow(ADI_CT_Data)),1), "%)", sep = "")

ADI_C_Data <- ADI_C_Data[!is.na(ADI_C_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI),]
disc_20 <- sum(ADI_C_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI <= -20 | ADI_C_Data$Diff_NA_ReADI >= 20, na.rm = T) 
paste(round(disc_20, 1), " of ", round(nrow(ADI_C_Data), 1), " (", round(100*(disc_20/nrow(ADI_C_Data)),1), "%)", sep = "")
```
